items.description: 文宇奶酪（南锣鼓巷店）是南锣鼓巷内的具体奶酪甜品门店。大众点评图片页显示，该店有原味奶酪、双皮奶、奶卷等菜品分类及价目表照片，但未提供可核实的当前菜单、价格或营业状态。北京旅游官方页面曾记载其位于南锣鼓巷49号，并称店主“据说”师承三元梅园，实行每日限量销售；这些属于报道中的历史或传述，不能替代现场核实。
items.editor_note: 资料由平台商户图片页与北京旅游官方页面取得，二者分别提供菜品分类、店铺描述及旧地址信息。官方页面使用“据说”等传述性表述，不能据此认定本店建筑年代或当前营业情况；现场经营状况、价格和体验项目未知。

items.description: 方砖厂69号炸酱面（方砖厂胡同店）为方砖厂胡同内的具体经营门店。大众点评相册页将本店地址列为方砖厂胡同1号，人均信息为27元；“69号”属于品牌名称，不是该页面列出的门牌。北京旅游报道则称其连续六年获米其林指南推荐，并被列入相关消费地图，但这是报道转述，不能据此确认当前经营或本店建筑历史。

items.description: 景秀餐厅（南锣鼓巷店）是南锣鼓巷片区的具体餐饮门店。携程商户页列出地址为南锣鼓巷东棉花胡同36号，并展示北京菜、碎溜鸡、水煮鱼等菜品；该页面同时显示营业时间和“营业中”状态，但属于平台快照，不能代表当前营业。北京旅游报道称其始于1992年并被称为“中戏第二食堂”，这里只作为店史报道，不推定现存房屋建于1992年。

items.en: Wenyu Cheese (Nanluoguxiang Branch) is a specific cheese-dessert shop on Nanluoguxiang. The Dianping photo page shows categories and price-list photos for items such as original-flavor cheese, double-skin milk, and milk rolls, but does not provide verifiable current menu, prices, or operating status. A Beijing tourism official page once recorded its address as No. 49 Nanluoguxiang and stated that the owner was “said to have learned from” Sanyuan Meiyuan, with sales limited daily; these are historical reports or hearsay and cannot replace on-site verification.

Fangzhuanchang No. 69 Zhajiangmian (Fangzhuanchang Hutong Branch) is a specific operating shop in Fangzhuanchang Hutong. The Dianping album page lists the shop address as No. 1 Fangzhuanchang Hutong and the per-person information as CNY 27; “No. 69” is part of the brand name, not the street number listed on that page. A Beijing tourism report stated that it had been recommended by the Michelin Guide for six consecutive years and included on a relevant consumption map, but this is reported information and cannot confirm current operation or the building’s history.

Jingxiu Restaurant (Nanluoguxiang Branch) is a specific dining establishment in the Nanluoguxiang area. The Ctrip merchant page lists the address as No. 36 Dongmianhua Hutong, Nanluoguxiang, and displays dishes such as Beijing cuisine, suiliu chicken, and boiled fish; the page also shows business hours and an “Open” status, but this is a platform snapshot and cannot represent current operation. A Beijing tourism report stated that it began in 1992 and was known as the “second cafeteria of the Central Academy of Drama”; here this is included only as a report on the shop’s history and does not imply that the existing building was built in 1992.

Beiping Garden · Chaowan Mengya · Beiping Coffee (Nanluoguxiang Hutong Branch) is a specific coffee and dining establishment presented under a combined name. The shop’s platform page lists coffee, waffles, pizza, pasta, desserts, and other items; the Ctrip page uses another combined name that includes a youth hostel and provides the address No. 113-2 Nanluoguxiang along with platform operating information. This entry only organizes dining information for the shop and does not expand to the youth hostel’s accommodation business.

Tangfang Coffee (Nanluoguxiang Branch) is a coffee shop in the Nanluoguxiang area. The Dianping page categorizes it under “Nanluoguxiang/Gulou East Street Coffee”; the snapshot shows a platform rating of 4.3 and an average per-person spending of CNY 48, and lists latte, iced Americano, specialty pour-over coffee, flat white, and other user-recommended drinks. Pizza, pasta, and desserts are also listed. The available sources support only the shop category, consumption snapshot, and recommended-dish information shown on the platform page, and cannot confirm current operation, a complete menu, prices, or the customer experience.

Jingshanzi (Nanluoguxiang Branch) is a specialty shop selling fans, and design reporting also described it as a space where fan enthusiasts could drink tea, converse, and discuss the appreciation of fans. A 2018 design article stated that it was located at No. 6 Nanluoguxiang and described various fans displayed in the shop, with wood finishes as the display background and display stands and cabinets designed to the scale of the fans. The available Dianping source only confirms the shop name and the existence of a photo page; the old design report reflects the space at that time and cannot replace verification of the current displays or operating status.

Yiduo Yiguo (Nanluoguxiang Branch) is a shop selling journaling and stationery items, postcards, and related goods. An industry shop-visiting article described a Nanluoguxiang shop as a “journaling laboratory,” introducing its tapes, pens, notebooks, stamps, journaling decorations, and some cartoon merchandise, and mentioning on-site making experiences. The platform page records another branch address as No. 45 Nanluoguxiang, while an index excerpt also shows No. 41 Nanluoguxiang. Since the same brand has two shops on Nanluoguxiang, this entry does not combine goods or experiences associated with different street numbers.

Jiaque'er Handcrafted Cultural-Creative Shop (Nanluoguxiang), according to a Beijing culture and tourism report from March 2026, is a newly opened distinctive street-front shop on Nanluoguxiang. The report describes it as a handcrafted cultural-creative shop and mentions a cement-gray façade, as well as handmade ceramic bottles, wooden animal ornaments, hand-painted gourd pendants, and other goods; it also records visitors’ interest in purchasing items while browsing the shop. The source does not provide a complete street number, business hours, prices, or information on continued operation, so all these details require on-site verification.

Qingsong Zaowu (Nanluoguxiang Designer Co-creation Space) was introduced in a Beijing culture and tourism report from March 2026 as a small young-person-run shop and designer co-creation space. The report lists cultural-creative products in the space, including ceramics, paper cuttings, stamps, and hand-painted gourd pendants, and states that visitors select goods in the shop. The available materials only describe the goods and spatial positioning presented at the time of the report; they cannot confirm current operation, stock, prices, or whether handmade courses are offered, nor can they imply that all goods have intangible cultural heritage certification.

Chocolate Player (Nanluoguxiang) is a young-person-run shop featured in a Beijing culture and tourism report from March 2026. The report focuses on its creative products: chocolate models of the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at the Temple of Heaven, the Great Wall, and other forms. It states that the models are lifelike and that visitors can smell chocolate when approaching them, finding this novel.
